arch_aqualume_bubble_lift_a_v01.description: A full-height underwater civic elevator built around a transparent pressure-rated cylindrical shaft rather than an ordinary box cabin. The lift stands on a broad reef-safe foundation ring and is wrapped by evenly spaced structural pressure ribs. Two opposing docking portals use thick sliding glass doors, illuminated seal tracks, mechanical latches, and exterior emergency-release housings. Inside the shaft, a luminous current-drive core and bubble intake manifold create the visible rising-water column that carries the passenger capsule between districts. A waist-height control pedestal, directional current arrows, service conduits, pressure gauges, emergency red seal bands, and a reinforced roof docking collar make its operation readable from every angle. The silhouette must read instantly as vertical underwater transit, with open glass volume between ring ribs and visible mechanical systems at the base and roof.
arch_aqualume_bubble_lift_a_v01.designIntent: Aqualume's elevator equivalent: elegant civic infrastructure combining marine pressure engineering, bioluminescent navigation, visible water movement, and believable maintenance access. It must feel built for daily residents, not like a decorative aquarium or a glass box with bubbles pasted inside.
functionalNotes: doors and lift capsule remain separable for later animation
current-drive core and navigation strips remain separately materialed
clear passenger opening and capsule clearance
forbiddenShortcuts: rectangular building with a glowing panel
single glass cylinder without pressure structure
bubbles represented only by a texture
coral pasted randomly onto mechanical surfaces

gap-aqualume-airlock-conduit-straight-st.description: A straight enclosed connector for joining dry Aqualume interiors across wet exterior space. The primary form is a thick pressure-glass pedestrian tube running between two oversized circular docking collars. Each end has layered compression flanges, visible gasket seams, locking dogs, alignment keys, and a short reinforced transition throat that can mate cleanly with neighboring modules. Five external load-bearing pressure hoops wrap the span and connect to a lower service spine carrying current cables, drainage, oxygen lines, and inspection access. One side includes a recessed service hatch with latch hardware, pressure gauge, warning placard, and emergency isolation valve. A narrow illuminated floor strip and repeated directional icons preserve orientation without relying on color alone. The conduit must read as hollow traversable architecture with believable wall thickness, not a solid cylinder or a rectangular bridge wearing round end caps.
gap-aqualume-airlock-conduit-straight-st.designIntent: A repeatable modular glassway component that makes Aqualume's architecture visibly pressure-rated, serviceable, and safe while preserving long sightlines through the underwater city.
functionalNotes: forward connection direction follows the long depth axis
both docking collars share a repeatable socket diameter
floor guide and service spine remain distinct meshes
forbiddenShortcuts: end collars without gasket or locking hardware
random loose cables crossing the walking path
opaque tube that hides the city

elevated_road_support_a_v01.description: A tall engineered support assembly for TechTown's elevated vehicle lanes. It begins with a wide reinforced concrete crash footing and rises through a tapered composite-clad pier with a recessed inspection door, drainage outlet, service conduit, and protected maintenance ladder. A broad transverse cap beam at the top carries four replaceable elastomeric bearing pads, two lateral restraint blocks, expansion-joint catch trays, and visible bolted access plates beneath the roadway deck. Diagonal steel knee braces connect the pier to the cap beam and create a recognizable load path instead of leaving a slab floating on a column. Low collision guards and reflective hazard bands protect the base at street level. Controlled cyan inspection lights may accent access points, but the structure remains primarily concrete, dark metal, and black composite.
elevated_road_support_a_v01.designIntent: Believable cyberpunk civil engineering. The support should look capable of carrying heavy traffic and being inspected or repaired, while maintaining a strong tapered silhouette readable beneath elevated roads.
functionalNotes: road deck bearings remain individually named
simple pier and cap-beam collision can be generated separately
ladder and inspection side face the service walkway
base leaves pedestrian clearance outside collision guards
forbiddenShortcuts: bearings painted onto the cap beam

gap-shared-world-accessibility-gate-lock.description: A clearly locked but accessibility-compliant pedestrian passage gate used across Zaylins facilities and restricted routes. Two anchored vertical posts frame a full-width gate leaf with rounded horizontal rails and closely spaced lower infill that prevents unsafe gaps without becoming visually prison-like. A heavy hinge barrel, lower pivot, and overhead closing arm show how the gate moves. The locked state is communicated by a visible mechanical latch, shielded electric strike, raised padlock icon, amber status lamp, and a physical CLOSED tab, so players do not have to rely on color. The approach side includes a large wheelchair-height push plate, tactile icon panel, card reader, intercom button, and emergency override housing. A flush threshold strip preserves wheelchair passage when unlocked. Lock actuator, gate leaf, and indicators remain separate for later state animation and quest logic.
gap-shared-world-accessibility-gate-lock.designIntent: A universal, readable locked-route object that communicates restriction without blocking accessibility design. It should feel like modern public-building hardware, not a tiny fence, jail gate, or abstract state cube.

push plate center is mounted at accessible reach height
